item.title: What we lose when we stop being able to tell
item.dc:creator: Ho Chin Wei
item.description:
Open with the claim, not the background. One short paragraph that tells the reader what the post argues, so they can decide in ten seconds whether to keep going. Assume they have not read anything else on this site.

Then the second paragraph does the setup — why the question matters, what the usual framing gets wrong. Prose runs at a 68-character measure and is justified, so paragraphs of three to six sentences sit better than very long or very short ones.

The usual framing

Use ## for sections. Each one gets a hairline rule above it, which is what gives a long post its rhythm — so use them generously, roughly every three or four paragraphs, and give them real titles rather than “Background” or “Discussion”.

Inline formatting works as you’d expect: emphasis, strong, inline code, and a link. A footnote goes like this1 and collects at the bottom of the post.

A pull quote is a hairline on the left and larger type. Use one when a sentence is worth stopping on — not to break up text you think is boring.

A sub-point

### is available for a level below, though most posts don’t need it.

Something worth flagging

NoteA note to one side

Callouts render as a hairline box with an accent rule on the left. .callout-note is the neutral one; .callout-warning, .callout-important and .callout-tip all work and look the same in this theme. Good for a methodological caveat or an aside that would derail the paragraph.

Showing your work

If the post needs numbers, write the chunk and let it run — the output is framed automatically and the code block keeps its highlighting:

# Any R works here. Keep chunks short enough to read on screen.
summary(cars$speed)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
    4.0    12.0    15.0    15.4    19.0    25.0

Plots get a caption and are matted like a photograph. fig-cap writes the caption; fig-alt is the screen-reader description and is worth filling in:

plot(cars$speed, cars$dist,
     pch = 16, col = "#4b7a55",
     xlab = "Speed (mph)", ylab = "Stopping distance (ft)")

Refer to it in the text as Figure 1 and Quarto numbers and links it for you.

An ordinary image, if you want one without R:

Closing

Land the argument. One paragraph, no summary of what you just said — say the thing you were building toward, or the question you’re leaving open.

How to use this file

Copy the whole template-post/ folder, rename it to a slug (blog/detection-is-the-wrong-test/), replace the front matter and the body, and delete this last section. The folder name becomes the URL. Keep each post’s images inside its own folder so a post stays self-contained.

Footnotes

  1. Footnotes are good for the caveat you don’t want in the main sentence.↩︎
